question: Should RFC maintainers sponsor the proposed Host-owned core split, including its automatic compatibility placement and owner-scoped restart/configuration contract, as accepted OpenClaw architecture direction?
rationale: The document is technically coherent, but choosing the permanent runtime ownership model and compatibility guarantees is a product and architecture decision that cannot be inferred from repository mechanics.

options.title: Continue the draft discussion
options.body: Keep the PR open as a draft while maintainers review the ownership model, compatibility guarantees, and rollout gates in the required discussion thread.

options.title: Narrow the RFC
options.body: Limit acceptance to logical ownership separation and defer process splitting, Connector v2, and permanent compatibility policy to follow-up RFCs.

options.title: Accept the full direction
options.body: Sponsor the complete Host, Control Server, and Channel Gateway architecture after explicitly approving its upgrade and plugin compatibility obligations.

recommendation.title: Continue the draft discussion
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open as a draft while maintainers review the ownership model, compatibility guarantees, and rollout gates in the required discussion thread.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history connects this person to the repository's RFC process and template, making them the best routing candidate for the required discussion and disposition.
